newsitem.title: POLAND: Politics may delay Polish pension reform - minister.
newsitem.headline: Politics may delay Polish pension reform - minister.

text.p: Poland's crucial reform of its inefficient social security system may fail to take off this year as planned because of party bickering, Labour Minister Tadeusz Zielinski said on Friday.

"Political considerations are standing in the way (of the reform). I have appealed not to make the social security reform an object of political bargaining, but it has already started," Zielinski told a news conference.
Asked whether two pivotal bills, which would kick off the reform, will become law before parliamentary elections, due after August, Zielinski said: "This is a great unknown."

The bills pave the way for the creation of new privately managed pension funds and endowing them with shares of firms undergoing privatisation. The funds would take part of the burden of providing social security from the subsidised state-owned Social Security Office (ZUS).

International financial organisations have warned that Poland's public finances face collapse in the long term if the reform is not carried out. The aging population would increase state subsidies to the system beyond what could be borne.
Zielinski declined to elaborate on how political considerations had and would hinder the reform. "Keep your eyes open and you will see," he said.

Analysts say several politicians in the ruling leftist coalition of ex-communists and a peasant party feared the launch of the reform in an election year would cost them the votes of those who would lose out on the changes.
The overhaul would most likely cut state subsidy to farmers' pensions and roll back privileges of some groups such as miners or the military, analysts say.
Zielinski said the ministry had drafted the two reform bills but he did not know when they would be submitted for the full cabinet's approval and then to parliament.
It is hard to say how much time government experts and cross-ministry bodies will need to clear the bills, he said.

The previous labour minister Andrzej Baczkowski, who died of heart attack last November after months of stressful work on the reform -- promised to send the two bills to parliament by the end of March.
Zielinski pledged to continue his predecessor's work but said he was not sure if the March deadline would be met.
